newsitem.title: USA: St. Mary to operate 50 U.S. wells in 1997.
newsitem.headline: St. Mary to operate 50 U.S. wells in 1997.

text.p: St. Mary Land & Exploration Co said Tuesday it plans in 1997 to double the number of wells it operates to 50 and to participate in an additional 60 to 75 wells operated by others on holdings located primarily in the Midcontinental United States.
"In 1997 St. Mary's exploration and development programs will test the largest and highest quality inventory of prospects in the Company's history," said president and CEO Mark Hellerstein.
"This could be an outstanding year because we will drill an unusually large number of our higher-risk, large-target exploration prospects," he said.

Hellerstein said in addition to the "significant discoveries" during the first quarter at South Horseshoe Bayou and Roanoke the company expect two "large-target" prospects in South Louisiana and one in the Sherman-Marietta Basin will be tested during the remainder of the year.

The company announced first quarter earnings from domestic operations of $5,296,000 or $0.55 cents per share, vs $468,000 or $0.05 cents in the comparable 1996 quarter. Revenues from domestic operations increased to $21.2 million in the first three months of 1997 as compared to $11.4 million in the same period of 1996.

St. Mary also recorded a pre-tax gain of $9,691,000 on the sale and exchange of its Russian interests in February, which combined with the record results of the company's ongoing domestic operations resulted in total revenues for the quarter of $30.9 million and net income of $11.6 million, or $1.20 per share.

Average daily domestic oil and gas production during the first quarter was 13,423 barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) as compared to 8,945 BOE and 11,306 BOE, respectively in the first and fourth quarters of 1996.
Barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by six and adding it to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.

Average prices realized during the quarter were $20.37 per barrel and $2.74 per thousand cubic feet (Mcf), 16 percent and 32 percent higher, respectively, than prices prevailing in the first quarter one year ago.
